headline: Backlog conversion lifts profit, margins expand
summary_short: TechnipFMC posted Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2,763M, up 9.0% y/y on Subsea backlog conversion, with segment operating profit up 30.2% and net income up 34.6% to $363M ($0.90 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.0% y/y to $2,763M on a $270.6M Subsea increase, as 17.4% higher year-end backlog converted into iEPCI®/SPS activity across Latin America, Asia Pacific, Africa and the Middle East, partly offset by weaker Europe/North America. Gross profit rose 15.4% to $685M on $62.8M volume gains plus $42.1M favorable mix. Segment operating profit rose 30.2% to $526M; Subsea margin expanded 2.4pts to 19.6%. Effective tax rate fell to 24.0% from 28.4% on geographic mix. Net income rose 34.6% to $363M ($0.90 diluted EPS). TechnipFMC repurchased $420.1M of shares, paid a $0.05/share dividend, and lifted net cash to $589.9M as cash rose to $992M and total debt fell to $402M. No forward guidance is stated in the filing.

drivers.explanation: The 10-Q attributes the quarter's profit growth to Subsea backlog conversion into higher-margin iEPCI/SPS activity, favorable volume and mix, and a lower effective tax rate.

Driven by a $270.6M Subsea revenue increase from 17.4% higher year-end 2025 backlog, led by Latin America, Asia Pacific, Africa and the Middle East, partly offset by lower Europe/North America activity.
Subsea gross profit rose $104.8M, of which $62.8M was due to volume increase and $42.1M to favorable activity mix, per the filing.
Subsea operating profit rose $106.2M on higher volume ($62.8M) and favorable mix ($42.1M); operating margin expanded 2.4 points to 19.6%.

Not explained in the release as a distinct line; the shard's Yahoo-sourced EBIT ($486.9M) differs by $7.1M from the 10-Q's own "income before net interest expense and income taxes" ($479.8M), unreconciled in the filing.
Not a filing-labeled line; the increase is consistent with the operating income gain against a broadly stable depreciation and amortization base.
Tracks the $121.8M segment operating profit gain plus a $10.8M drop in net interest expense from lower outstanding debt, partly offset by $8.0M higher other expense from FX remeasurement.
Follows the pretax income increase; the effective tax rate fell to 24.0% from 28.4%, which the filing attributes to the geographic distribution of earnings.
Mirrors the net income increase; diluted weighted-average shares fell to 404.5M from 420.5M as the quarter's $420.1M share repurchase reduced the share count.
Operating cash flow rose $94.6M YTD on higher net income and working-capital timing, partly offset by $684.9M YTD share repurchases and debt repayments, per the filing.
Total debt fell as the company continued scheduled repayments (six-month debt repayments of $15.0M vs. $241.6M a year earlier), per the filing.
Roughly flat y/y as retained-earnings growth from net income was largely offset by $684.9M of YTD share repurchases and cancellations.
